segments.t: The File Browser is a dockable sidebar that browses your KTPH000localKTPH001 filesystem next to the terminal. It shows a directory tree with a navigation toolbar, a path bar, a filter, type-aware icons and a status footer. (For browsing a KTPH002remoteKTPH003 server over SFTP, use the KTPH004SFTP file managerKTPH005 instead.)
Toggle the panel from the menu bar:
KTPH000View → File Browser → Show on LeftKTPH001
KTPH000View → File Browser → Show on RightKTPH001

Selecting the item again hides the panel. A draggable divider resizes it (160–420 px). The panel's KTPH000position, width, "show hidden" state and last directory are remembered across restartsKTPH001.
The toolbar and path bar drive where the tree is rooted:
Return to a previously visited directory
Root the tree at the parent directory (may go above your home directory)
Root the tree at your home directory
Reload the current directory, keeping expanded folders open
Create an item in the selected (or current) directory
Choose the sort key (Name, Size, Date modified) and direction (Ascending / Descending)

The KTPH001path barKTPH002 accepts a typed path and roots the tree there. A leading KTPH000 expands to your home directory; absolute paths outside home are allowed. The KTPH003filterKTPH004 field below it narrows the listing to entries whose name contains the typed text (case-insensitive).
Directories load in the background, so a large or network-mounted folder no longer freezes the window; a brief loading indicator appears while a directory is read.
Open a file, or expand/collapse a folder
Go up to the parent directory
Delete the selection (choose Trash or permanent)
Right-click an entry for the full menu:
KTPH000OpenKTPH001 — open the file with the operating system's default application.
KTPH000Open in Snippet EditorKTPH001 — load a text file (up to 10 MB) into the KTPH002Snippet EditorKTPH003.
KTPH002RenameKTPH003 — rename inline; a name clash is resolved by appending KTPH000, KTPH001, …
KTPH000CopyKTPH001 / KTPH002CutKTPH003 / KTPH004PasteKTPH005 — move or copy within the browser.
KTPH000Copy PathKTPH001 — copy the item's absolute path to the clipboard.

KTPH000DeleteKTPH001 — a confirmation prompt offers KTPH002Move to TrashKTPH003 or KTPH004Delete PermanentlyKTPH005. Moving to the Trash is reversible; permanent deletion cannot be undone. On a system without a Trash, only permanent deletion is offered. The deletion runs in the background so a large folder does not freeze the window.
KTPH000New FolderKTPH001 / KTPH002New FileKTPH003 — create an item.
KTPH000Set owner / group / permissionsKTPH001 — change ownership and POSIX permissions (where the filesystem supports it).
KTPH003ArchiveKTPH004 — pack the selection into a KTPH000, KTPH001 or KTPH002 archive.
KTPH000DetailsKTPH001 — show type, size, path, modification time and permissions.

Each row shows a KTPH000type-aware iconKTPH001 (folder, code, image, archive, document or executable), with a badge for symbolic links. The footer reports how many folders and files the current directory holds and how many entries are selected.

Drag files KTPH001outKTPH002 of the browser onto another application to copy them, and drag files KTPH003intoKTPH004 the browser to copy or move them into a folder. Dropping onto a folder targets that folder; dropping elsewhere targets the current directory. Name clashes are resolved with a KTPH000 suffix rather than overwriting.
